work_packages.name: Every pixel of the valley carries correct motion under jitter, including the sky and stars

items.statement: The view record carries the jitter offset from a continuous 32-phase Halton(2,3) sequence, jittered and unjittered matrices, the previous submitted unjittered matrices, the mip bias and the subrectangle; (0,0) never occurs, and the record layout matches the changed RENDER-SPEC.
items.ask: Do tests in ./dev check assert the sequence values, the absence of (0,0) and the record layout byte for byte, and does RENDER-SPEC state the same layout with its design hash refreshed? Do the previous matrices come from the last submitted frame, not the last encoded one?

items.statement: Motion is computed from unjittered clip positions: a static scene under jitter reads back zero motion everywhere.
items.ask: Does the test read the real motion target back from the GPU over several jitter phases and fail on any nonzero texel, with a moving-object control that must be nonzero?

items.statement: The sky, Sun disk and stars write motion at infinity including the celestial phase delta; under a known camera pan the sky's motion matches the expected value within 0.05 px.
items.ask: Is the expected sky motion derived independently of the shader, does the test cover a time step with the camera still (phase delta only), and is the change inside the atmosphere shaders limited to motion output as the module list's seam 4 ruling says?

items.statement: Objects with invalid history are marked as such, ready for the reactive target, instead of writing a fabricated zero vector: a spawn, a camera cut, a device replacement and a cooked asset swap each mark their geometry.
items.ask: For each of the four cases, where is the mark set and where is it cleared, and can any drawer in the forward pass (synthetic, contribution, cooked on both draw paths) still emit zero motion for geometry with no previous position?

items.statement: A motion view in the existing display pass shows motion on the valley route: during a pan, terrain, objects, sky and stars all move in the expected direction with magnitudes that grow sensibly from the pan's centre to its edge.
items.inspect: Capture a pan on the valley route with the motion view on, as a fixed-time sequence from the Mac engine capture. Watch it in motion and check whole frames and crops of: the skyline, a near object against far terrain, the star field at night, and a moving object. Say that you watched motion.

work_packages.quality_bar: Motion fit to drive a shipped temporal reconstructor such as MetalFX or Unreal's TSR: zero for a static scene under jitter, exact at infinity for the sky, Sun and stars, and marked invalid where there is no history rather than fabricated. Judged on the current portable output, before any reconstruction exists.

work_packages.name: Depth, motion, reactive and exposure are stored for reconstruction, and history advances only with submitted frames

items.statement: With reconstruction enabled, depth and motion are stored and sampleable, and APPLE-TILE's eligibility report shows them stored; with it disabled nothing extra is stored.
items.ask: Does the eligibility report from APPLE-TILE WP1 list depth and motion as stored only when a reader exists, and is the disabled path's attachment storage unchanged from before this work package?

items.statement: A third forward target, reactive R8Unorm, is declared by every forward drawer: synthetic, scene contribution, cooked direct and indirect, the sky, and the separate star pass, whose attachments and graph accesses match its shader outputs; their pipeline tests pass.
items.ask: Does every forward drawer declare the third target, including the cooked direct and indirect paths with their COOKED-DRAW selection and history rules intact, and does the star pass attach and declare access to every target its shader writes? Does a contribution get the target through the contribution seam rather than a private binding?

items.statement: Each frame resolves a 1x1 R16Float exposure texture, and the history sample retains the storage scale it was written with.
items.ask: Does a test change the storage scale between two frames and show the history sample rescaled correctly rather than reinterpreted?

items.statement: History follows submission order: with two frames in flight and a held submission the history sample advances at each successful submission; the previous matrices are the last submitted frame's; a forced submission failure resets history; a frame cancelled on failed acquisition leaves history at the last submitted frame; an iOS background drop resets it; HistoryKey uses the output extent.
items.ask: Read the pipelined tests. Is each of the six clauses asserted separately on the real frame host, are the cancelled-acquisition and background-drop cases counted in the proof log, and does the existing presentation-drop contract behave as before?

items.statement: In Chrome, on the game's own frame path, rows WP1-W7 of the design's temporal-input witness hold: reactive is written where history is invalid and cleared where it is valid, and the frame after an unsubmitted view takes the last submitted frame as its predecessor, in identity and in the motion it writes.
items.ask: Read the temporal case. Are the reactive and motion values taken from frames the page submitted, not from a side render or a declaration? Is the unsubmitted view abandoned at the latest point the browser frame path allows, with the predecessor identity read from the state the previous matrices are packed from? Would a reactive target that is never written, and history advanced before submission, each fail a row?

items.statement: On the Mac, rows WP1-W5 of the design's temporal-input witness hold, read back from the reactive target itself: 1 on invalid-history geometry and 0 once valid, the volume's alpha on the cooked volume, above 0 on stars and the Sun disk on a phase edit, and 0 for steady stars and uncovered pixels.
items.ask: Do GPU tests drive the witness fixture through the real forward and star passes, read the reactive target back, and assert each of WP1-W5 against the expected values in the fixture definition that the Chrome case also reads?

items.statement: With the third target declared, the browser checker's existing cases still pass in Chrome. This is a regression check only; it proves nothing about reactive values or history.

work_packages.quality_bar: The temporal inputs and acceptance rules a shipped reconstructor relies on: history that never includes a frame the display did not get, and reactive marking wherever history cannot be trusted. Correctness only; nothing visible changes yet.

work_packages.name: TAAU reconstructs the valley at native scale in the game, on the Mac and in Chrome

items.statement: TAAU runs at scale 1.0 in the V1 game on the Mac with the portable recipe forced and in Chrome, on the route; the present path reads TAAU's linear output through APPLE-TILE's pre-tone input and the existing SDR transform still runs once.
items.ask: Is the reconstructor resolved from the registry with TAAU as the portable default, and does its output enter only through the pre-tone input APPLE-TILE WP3 delivered, with no second tone or exposure step?

items.statement: At each still route checkpoint the design's reconstruction reference exists (the 32 jitter offsets at native resolution, averaged with the scene, time and exposure held), and TAAU's p99 colour difference to it meets the design's reconstruction tolerance and is lower than the no-AA frame's at the same checkpoint.
items.ask: Read the reconstruction arm. Is the reference accumulated by a separate mode from the TAAU path it judges, with the held state checked and not assumed? Is the difference the design's CIEDE2000 over the whole frame without masks, against the bound the design states? Does a deliberately broken TAAU (history disabled) fail?

items.statement: On the Mac, motion sequences show no ghosting or crawl: pans and translating lights, a reveal behind a moving prop, a spawn, a held-camera star field with no shimmer, and a time-of-day scrub with no brightness lag.
items.inspect: Capture each of the five sequences with the Mac real-time engine capture, TAAU on, and the same sequences with it off. Judge each from its captured frames, as the design's motion review says: runs of consecutive frames in their captured order and timing, on beside off, in native-size crops of trailing edges, the revealed background, the spawned object's first frames, individual stars, and the sky during the scrub. An agent judges this, with no playback and no human observer (owner, 18 November 2026: "agents can judge"). Say which frames you read for each of the five.

items.statement: In Chrome the same five sequences show no ghosting, crawl, shimmer or brightness lag.
items.inspect: Capture the five sequences with Chrome real-time capture, TAAU on and off, and judge the same crops the same way, from the captured frames. Say which frames you read for each of the five, and note any sequence where Chrome differs from the Mac.

items.statement: A camera cut shows no prior history on the next frame: the frame after the cut equals a frame rendered with history reset.
items.ask: Does the cut arm compare the post-cut frame with an independently reset render, and does a control with the reset suppressed fail?

items.statement: TAAU's GPU time on the route is recorded at WP3's own 640x360 extent, kept apart from the design's 1080p estimate, with build, load and order; a departure from the estimate is recorded as a tripwire, not a failure.
items.ask: Is the timing a paired on/off record on the route at the stated extent, labelled for load, and is it kept from being read as the 1080p figure the design estimates?

work_packages.quality_bar: Antialiasing as stable as a shipped game's temporal AA at native scale: clean edges and thin features on the held route, no ghosting behind moving things, no crawl on stars or foliage-thin geometry, no brightness lag as time of day changes. Judged in motion from the running game on portable, in words.

work_packages.name: The valley fills the window at any size, and keeps presenting while the window is resized

items.statement: On the Mac, on both native recipes, the render extent is the window's backing size: at 1280×720 and 1920×1080 points and at full screen the submitted frame covers every backing pixel with no band, one render pixel to one output pixel at scale 1.0, and no host is created at the old fixed 640×360 unless a caller names that extent.
items.ask: Does the arm read the submitted frame through engine capture's tap at each size, and compare the extent the host resolved with the window's backing size? Do offscreen, capture and exact-baseline paths still name their own extents, so that no retained image moved?

items.statement: On the iPhone simulator the render extent follows the oriented surface in portrait and in landscape, and the band and the moiré the G3b route recorded are gone. Function only.
In Chrome the render extent is the canvas's backing size at device pixel ratios of 1 and 2, follows a canvas resize, and the first frame at a new size carries no history from the old one.

Through a resize driven by a scripted clock, the host presents the old generation at its own extent, and makes no call on the surface, until the new one is ready. A build starts when the extent has been stable for the debounce, on the preparation thread. A newer extent cancels a running build, whose result is never bound. Each generation the host takes is one successful configure call, to that generation's extent and in the step that takes it. The render thread creates no texture, view, bind group or pipeline at any point.
items.ask: Read the test. Does it drive the host's own resize and frame calls, count creations by thread, and include a control in which the build runs on the render thread and the count sees it? Is a superseded build's result shown never to reach a frame?

items.statement: A finished build is taken only if it was made for the current device generation and the latest request. Device loss during a build drops the build, and recovery starts a new one. A build that fails leaves the old generation presenting and is reported. The old generation is retired only when its frames in flight have completed. History resets in the first frame of the new generation and in no other frame of the transition.
items.ask: Read the test. Is each of the four cases driven through the host's own calls, and is the history reset shown by comparing the first new frame with an independently reset one, with a control that keeps history across the switch failing?

items.statement: In the Mac game window, on both native recipes, a resize sweep made in code and a forced backing-scale change on the display record each keep frames presenting throughout, the old generation at its own extent until the new one is ready. Each generation taken is one successful configure call, the sweep makes no other call on the surface, and no switch needs a restore. Each frame's record carries the window's backing size beside the surface's extent, and each switch's record carries its deferrals and its calls. Every display tick without a present during the sweep carries its reason in the frame record: none is a wait for a build, and a wait for the GPU appears only inside a configure call, with its duration. Render-thread frame times through the sweep are on record beside the run without one, a spike is flagged as a tripwire, and no time decides the result.
items.ask: Does the arm resize a real game window and read the engine's frame records, with the console state recorded as a witness and not as a pass condition? Does it fail when the transition is forced back to the synchronous path, which reconfigures at every step?

items.statement: On the Mac a resize reads cleanly in the window itself. While the edge moves, the old picture fills the window, scaled smoothly, with no band or blank area. The switch to the new size is one clean change in the window, with no black frame, flash, half-drawn frame or ghost of the old picture, and no hold on the last frame long enough to read as a freeze.
items.inspect: Record the game window itself through the resize sweep and the backing-scale change with OS-window capture, on one native recipe, with the display held awake. Read runs of consecutive captured window frames from while the size changes, and the run across every switch from the last scaled frame to the first at the new size: the picture fills the window in each, and the change is one step. Capture the same two changes with T2 engine capture in `realtime` mode on each native recipe, and judge the frames around every switch whole and in native-size crops of the terrain silhouette, the grid fixture and a thin prop. Name the frames read.

needs.what: Screen Recording granted to the tool that captures the game window, with the Mac unlocked. The agent wakes the display, runs the capture and reviews it; nobody has to watch.

items.statement: A switch is entered only at a frame boundary with no surface texture held and no job on the preparation thread. Otherwise it is deferred: the host makes no configure call, keeps the ready generation, presents the old one and takes the switch at a later boundary. A configure error is followed, before the host acquires again, by one restoring call with the old generation's configuration. The ready generation is then dropped unbound, the old one presents, and the error is reported with its request. If the restore fails too, the host acquires nothing until a later configure succeeds. Deferrals, configure calls, generations taken and restores are counted apart.
items.ask: Read the test. Does its surface behave as released wgpu does after an error, reporting the size it was asked for while the drawable keeps the old one, so that a host which skipped the restore would fail? Is a deferral shown to make no call, and is each of the four counts asserted for a deferred switch, a failed one with a good restore and a failed one with a failed restore?

items.statement: On a real wgpu surface on the Mac, a switch whose configure call fails inside wgpu leaves one answer for the drawable's size. The fault is one that leaves wgpu-core's old presentation in place, such as a configuration it rejects or a submission that lands in its wait. After the host's restore, the next surface texture reports the size Metal gives for its drawable, which is the old generation's extent, and that frame presents. The same run with the restore skipped shows the two sizes disagree.
items.ask: Is the error raised by wgpu's own configure, through the host's switch, and not by a test double? Is the drawable's size read from Metal and not from wgpu's descriptor?

items.statement: On the iPhone simulator, through real rotations from portrait to landscape and back, the owner takes no drawable under the new epoch until the surface is configured to the new extent, and presents nothing between the resize and the new extent's first frame except the one raced present the lease allows. No other present has a drawable whose size differs from the observed extent. The first present after each resize is at the new extent under the current epoch, within the route's bound of six frame replies. PID, window, lease and device generation are kept. Function only.

work_packages.quality_bar: A window that behaves as a shipped Mac game's does: the picture fills it at the display's own pixel size, with no band and no blocky scaling, and dragging its edge never freezes or blanks the picture, as in Baldur's Gate 3 or Resident Evil Village on macOS. Judged from the running game on the Mac, with Chrome and the iPhone simulator for function.

work_packages.name: The retained native valley images reflect the corrected material mip bias

items.statement: The `apple-tile-native` references affected by the native spatial mip bias restored in `32dfd3c14` match fresh registered captures for both Metal recipes. Both module logs record the cause and every replaced file's old and new SHA-256. The reference guard and the exact-images verifier pass under the native mip-bias ruling.
items.ask: Do the matched captures show the bias change accounts for the replaced references, starting with `portable-sdr-approach`? Do the candidate verification record, both logs and the landing diff agree on the files and hashes, the `apple-tile-native` pin and refresh, and the unchanged comparison and capture settings?

work_packages.name: A small exposure check catches a twilight brightness rebound
work_packages.quality_bar: Keep the original regression coverage with the smallest fixture that exposes it and ample headroom in the fast tier.

items.statement: The twilight test stays in the fast tier and still proves that physical sky radiance falls and that displayed sky luminance falls with it through the incident meter and low-light adaptation. Guard: the twilight exposure regression on a compact GPU target.
items.ask: Does the evidence account for every test listed in the plan, and do its fast cases retain the original assertions, boundary cases and tolerances at the smaller scale? Do the alone and focused batch runs show margin below the ten-second limit?

work_packages.name: Render scale steps during play with no hitch and no history reset

items.statement: On the route with TAAU the scale steps through 1.0, 0.85, 0.75, 0.67 and 0.5 during play, on the Mac's portable recipe. No step resets history: the frame after each step differs from a history-reset frame, and a control that resets history at the step is detected by the same comparison.
items.ask: Read the scale arm. Is the frame after a step compared with an independently reset render of the same state, and is the jitter sequence shown to continue across the step?

items.statement: A scale change creates no texture, view, bind group or pipeline on any thread: the creation counters are flat across every step, with attachments allocated once at scale 1.0.
items.ask: Read the test. Does a control that reallocates at a step make the counters move?

items.statement: At every scale, motion, the sky, aerial lookups and reconstruction address the drawn subrectangle only: WP1's zero-motion and sky-pan witnesses hold, a border outside the subrectangle filled with a marker colour changes no output pixel, and material sampling uses the mip bias log2(render/output) − 1 from the view record.
items.ask: Read the test. Is the marker border written into the attachments themselves, outside the subrectangle, at each of the five scales, and compared against a run without it over the whole output?

items.statement: At each still route checkpoint the design's colour difference to the reconstruction reference is on record for each of the five scales. Scale 1.0 still meets WP3's tolerance; no bound is set below it.
In Chrome the five steps run on the route with TAAU, with no history reset and no creation at a step.

On the Mac a step between any two neighbouring scales is not seen as an event: no hitch, flash or jump in the picture, and at 0.67 and 0.5 the terrain silhouette, the grid fixture and thin props are softer but do not break up, crawl or shimmer.
items.inspect: Capture the route with a scripted scale trace that visits every step, with T2 engine capture in `realtime` mode. Watch each step at 1x and judge native-size crops of the three features just before and after it. Say that you watched motion.

items.statement: On the Mac, GPU time for forward and sky, for TAAU and for the atmosphere is on record at each scale against the drawn area, from two separate runs with build and load. A departure from the design's cost account is flagged as a tripwire. No time decides the result.
items.ask: Does the command succeed or fail on the record being complete, and never on a time?

work_packages.quality_bar: Dynamic resolution as in a shipped game that hides it well, such as Spider-Man 2 or Forza Horizon 5: the picture softens a little at lower scale and never pops, flashes, shimmers at the step or loses its history. Judged in motion from the running game on the Mac and in Chrome.

work_packages.name: Chrome's SDR valley matches the retained frames again
work_packages.quality_bar: Match the registered APPLE-TILE records byte for byte. Meet WP6's float headroom and undithered H = 1 identity bounds on Metal.

items.statement: Chrome's fixed day SDR route matches all 481 retained record identities and decoded RGBA8 digests, including ordinal 61. The full exact-images matrix passes on main against the registered references.
items.ask: Do the matched Chrome control and corrected captures isolate the SDR shader change and recover all 481 records? Does the landing keep the reference files, registry, capture settings and comparator intact? Do the Metal D6.2 and D6.3 receipts on the corrected shader still meet the float headroom and H = 1 identity bounds?

work_packages.name: Highlights go brighter than SDR white on the built-in XDR display

items.statement: When a session starts on a display whose potential headroom is above 1, the game's surface is `Rgba16Float` in extended linear sRGB. The platform sets the layer's EDR properties on the main thread through a layer reference it keeps itself, never through wgpu's surface. The game can read the resolved display mode and the current headroom H.
items.ask: Where are `preferredDynamicRange` and `contentsHeadroom` set, on which thread, and through which reference to the layer? Does any path take wgpu's layer lock? Is the display's real record kept as a witness beside the forced one the arm uses?

items.statement: The EDR transform is the design's. On a CPU reference and in the shader, for exposed values from 0 to 2^18 and H of 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8 and 16: the output equals the SDR curve below the knee, never exceeds H, is continuous with a continuous slope at the knee, never decreases as a colour's largest channel grows, and at H = 1 is the SDR curve to float rounding.
items.ask: Read the test. Is the CPU reference written from the design's formula and not from the shader? Is the shader's output read back from a float target for the same inputs?

items.statement: With H forced to 1, the EDR branch's submitted frame, encoded to 8-bit sRGB without dither, is within one code of the SDR branch's undithered frame at every pixel of each still route checkpoint, on both native recipes.
items.ask: Are both frames taken from one scene state through engine capture's tap, and is the float frame the one the surface was given?

items.statement: A display record forced to a potential headroom of 1 keeps the EDR surface with H = 1, reconfigures nothing and creates no pipeline. A session started with EDR unavailable selects the prepared 8-bit surface at its generation build. A window on the 8-bit surface that reaches a display with potential headroom above 1 changes surface through a generation transition.
A forced change of current headroom reaches the present pass within one display tick with no creation, and no submitted pixel is ever above the record's current headroom.

On the route at H of 2 and 8, the float frame read through engine capture's tap has values above 1.0 on the Sun disk, in the sunset sky beside the Sun and on local lights, none above H, and every pixel whose exposed value is below the knee equals the H = 1 frame's.
items.ask: Does engine capture read the float target the surface was given in this mode, without changing what it records in the 8-bit mode?

items.statement: On the iPhone simulator the game runs the 8-bit SDR path, and a headroom value forced on the iOS display record reaches the render owner through the polling path without touching the surface lease.

In false colour and scaled down to SDR for viewing, the EDR frames at H of 2 and 8 show highlights that keep their colour and shape: the Sun's disc is round with a soft edge of sky around it, the sunset sky grades without a flat clipped patch or a band, and each lamp is a point with its own colour.
items.inspect: From the float captures of D6.6 make, for the sunset and the night-lights stops, a false-colour image of values above 1.0 and an image divided by H. Judge each whole and in native-size crops of the Sun, the sky beside it and two lamps, beside the SDR frame of the same state.

work_packages.quality_bar: HDR output as a shipped Mac game does it on an XDR display, such as Death Stranding or Resident Evil Village: the Sun, the sky beside it and lamps carry values above white and keep their colour and shape, while everything below the highlights is exactly the SDR picture. What the panel emits is the owner's to observe, and no item waits for that.

work_packages.name: The governor holds the display rate under forced load, then recovers step by step

items.statement: Driven by scripted frame samples in virtual time, the governor's policy lowers scale after three consecutive frames over budget, recovers at most one step in each minimum period, changes nothing while samples stay inside the budget, and takes its budget from the display interval so that a refresh change moves only the budget. It holds while a generation build runs, changing nothing and admitting no sample or missed tick from a frame encoded in the hold. It resumes after the first frame of a new generation, or at the next frame when the build ended with none (failed, or cancelled back to the current generation), with its committed values and an empty sample window, and lowers scale under load from then on.
items.ask: Read the test. Is the policy a function of samples, missed ticks, the display record and the host's hold marks alone, with no clock of its own? Is each behaviour a separate case with a control? After a build that ended with no new generation, is scale shown to drop under load with no further change of request?

items.statement: On the route on the Mac a forced GPU load from the debug-load pass makes the governor lower scale within its panic window, after which display ticks without a present return to the rate of the run without the load. When the load lifts, scale recovers one step in each minimum period. The trace is retained, and the frame record carries the governor's state: scale, tier, each knob's value and the reason for the last change.
items.ask: Are ticks without a present counted by the frame host from display-link ticks, and labelled as a render-side proxy? Does the arm fail with the governor off under the same load?

items.statement: With no forced load, the route on the Mac shows at most two scale changes, at the display rate the run records.
The world's state hash and tick count at the end of the route are identical with the governor on, off and under the forced load.

A crate outside `thrum-render` registers a quality knob through the public interface, a cadence or a step budget with its declared history invalidation, and the governor commits the knob's values between frames with no creation. The aerial lookup's cadence is registered through the same interface. A cadence change keeps effect histories and marks their age; a tier change resets the history of each effect whose algorithm it changes and no other. No knob changes simulation state or what a query returns.
items.ask: Read the test. Is registration open to a crate that `thrum-render` does not name, as the module list's quality-knobs interface requires for `WATERS` and `CLOUDS`? Does the test register a knob from a test contribution and watch its value change under load?

items.statement: A thermal state forced through the platform's record lowers the effect tier and the aerial cadence without creating a pipeline, and a return to nominal restores them step by step.

In Chrome the governor lowers scale under the forced load and recovers, from GPU timestamps where the page has them and from animation-frame intervals where it does not. The run records which it used.

In real time on the Mac, through the forced load and the recovery, the motion stays smooth and the picture shows no oscillation, pop or flash: a viewer who is not told cannot point to the frame of a scale step.
items.inspect: Capture the forced-load run with T2 engine capture in `realtime` mode, with capture's own cost shown apart. Watch it at 1x, then judge native-size crops of thin features across each step the trace names. Say that you watched motion.

items.statement: Through the frame host's own calls, a resize whose build is forced to fail leaves the old generation presenting, and with the request left unchanged a forced load then lowers the governor's scale and the load's lifting recovers it. The same is true after a build cancelled by a resize back to the current extent.
items.ask: Read the test. Is the failed build the one D4.5's test forces, reached through the host's resize and frame calls and not by setting the governor's state? Does a control whose hold never ends fail it?

work_packages.quality_bar: A frame-rate governor as steady as Unreal's dynamic resolution in a shipped game: under a sudden load the picture gets a little softer within a few frames and the motion stays smooth, quality returns slowly when the load lifts, nothing oscillates, and the simulation never notices.

work_packages.name: MetalFX reconstructs the valley on Apple tile, with TAAU as its prepared fallback

items.statement: On the Apple recipe the MetalFX temporal scaler runs inside the native segment on the route, at scales from 1.0 to 0.5. It is created with synchronous initialisation, in generation builds only; no native object is created during play; Metal's validation reports no error; and the game reports MetalFX as the resolved reconstructor.
items.ask: Is the scaler encoded on the native segment's own command buffer, as APPLE-TILE's boundary requires? Are creations counted by phase, with Metal's validation layer on for the run?

items.statement: A translating-object scene confirms the motion sign and scale and the jitter's Y sign: on the object's edges MetalFX's output follows TAAU's and the reference, and a control with either sign flipped fails.

Through a time-of-day scrub, and through a storage scale forced to step, MetalFX's frame is no further in mean luminance from the frame drawn without reconstruction than TAAU's is, beyond the noise the first run records between two identical runs. If the exposure texture alone does not meet that, the design's normalising pre-pass is on: it hands the pre-tone input its colour with the matching constant exposure, tone is unchanged, it clamps to the half-float range with its high clamps, low clamps and non-finite repairs counted, its GPU time is on record, and the game reports which path is in use.
items.ask: Was the noise floor recorded before either path was judged? With the pre-pass on, does any second exposure or tone step exist, does a still frame equal the frame without the pre-pass to within float rounding of the tone input, and is an exposed value just above 65504/K clamped to the largest finite half value and counted while one just below it is not?

items.statement: At each still route checkpoint, MetalFX's colour difference to the reconstruction reference is on record beside TAAU's at each of the five scales.
A forced provider rejection selects the prepared TAAU twin with no pipeline created, and the game reports TAAU with the reason.

A frame discarded after a failed acquisition resets the MetalFX provider before its next encode, and a failed submission and a generation change do the same. Each is counted beside the portable recipe's drop, and the frame after each equals a history-reset frame.
items.ask: Read the test. Is each of the three causes driven through the host's own calls, with a control that skips the reset failing?

items.statement: On the iPhone simulator a frame dropped in the background resets reconstruction history, and the drop is counted.
On the Mac's Apple recipe, WP3's five motion sequences and a sequence across a governor scale step show no ghosting, crawl, shimmer or brightness lag beyond TAAU's on the same sequence.
items.inspect: Capture each sequence with T2 engine capture in `realtime` mode with MetalFX and again with TAAU. Watch each pair at 1x and judge native-size crops of trailing edges, the revealed background, the spawned object's first frames, single stars and the sky during the scrub. Say that you watched motion.

work_packages.quality_bar: Upscaling as clean as MetalFX in a shipped Mac game, such as Resident Evil Village or Death Stranding: sharp at reduced scale, no ghosting behind moving things, no shimmer on stars or thin geometry, and no brightness lag as the time of day changes. At least as stable as this engine's own TAAU on the same sequences.

work_packages.name: Surface, device and display changes create nothing during play, and launch-to-ready time is on record

items.statement: Launch-to-ready on this Mac is on record cold, with the system's Metal shader cache for the game cleared, and warm, split into WGSL translation, MSL compilation and pipeline-state creation, with synchronous MetalFX creation apart, from two separate runs of each with build and load. The figures are baselines: no time decides the result.
items.ask: How does the arm clear the cache and show that the cold run was cold? Does the command succeed or fail on the record being complete, and never on a time?

items.statement: Each of these takes its designed path with no creation on the render thread and no pipeline compiled: a replaced surface; a forced refresh change, which moves only the governor's budget; a forced display move, which changes only H; and a resize while MetalFX is the reconstructor. A new device generation makes its pipelines again in recovery preparation, counted as its own phase, is ready before it draws, and compiles nothing after that readiness.
items.ask: Read the test. Is there one case for each of the five, each asserting the counters by thread and phase and the one thing the design says changes? Is readiness taken for each device generation, with recovery preparation counted apart from play?

items.statement: After readiness a whole route on each native recipe compiles no pipeline and creates no shader module: the counters after readiness are zero, and a control that builds one pipeline late is counted.
In Chrome a whole route creates no pipeline and no shader module after the page reports ready, counted where the page calls the device.

work_packages.quality_bar: As free of shader-compilation stutter as a shipped game that compiles its pipelines on a loading screen before play, as Horizon Zero Dawn and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare do on PC: after the game is ready, nothing is compiled, whatever the window or the display does, and a lost device is prepared again behind the same readiness before play resumes.

work_packages.name: Shaders compiled ahead of time load at launch with no WGSL translation, and pipelines are prepared in parallel

items.statement: Every pipeline on the route's manifest takes its shader from a Metal library cooked ahead of time, through passthrough, with no WGSL fallback in a parity run on both native recipes, and every still route checkpoint is byte for byte the frame the WGSL-built pipelines draw.
items.ask: Is the manifest the set of pipelines the route really creates, taken from the creation counters and not written by hand? Are fallbacks counted where the loader falls back?

items.statement: Through the pinned backend, a pipeline stage made from a cooked blob gets the stage record the WGSL path computes: the function's name, the workgroup size, the threadgroup memory lengths, the sized bindings and the immutable-buffer mask. A compute dispatch that uses threadgroup memory, and a stage that takes the length of a runtime-sized storage array, give the same results from a cooked blob as from WGSL, for a fixture and for the route's own `visibility.wgsl` and `atmosphere/diffuse.wgsl`. A blob with no record for the function is refused by name.
items.ask: Read the test. Do the Metal source and the record both come from the backend's own translation call, with no second implementation of its options? Would a backend that dropped the threadgroup lengths or the sized bindings fail it?

items.statement: A library is used only when its key matches what the running game would translate: the shader's source, the translator's version and options, and the Metal language version. On a mismatch the pipeline is built from WGSL before readiness and the fallback is counted; nothing is built from WGSL during play.
items.ask: Read the test. Is each part of the key changed in turn, and is the pipeline that results shown to draw?

items.statement: Pipelines are prepared across worker threads before readiness. With that on and off the set of pipelines ready is the manifest's, and launch-to-ready is on record for WGSL in series, cooked libraries, and cooked libraries prepared in parallel, cold and warm, from two separate runs of each with build and load. No time decides the result.
The library cook is a step of the cooker and the build, no shipping package links it, and Chrome's build and its checks are unchanged.
items.ask: Which package holds the cook, and does `scripts/g5_shipping_links.py` or its equal find it in no shipping package? Does the web bundle differ only where it must?

items.statement: The pinned copy of wgpu-hal is version 30.0.1 with the patch files kept beside it applied and nothing else, selected by a `[patch]` entry and registered in `.config/architecture.toml`. In WP10 its only patch is the passthrough stage record. The WGSL path translates and runs as in the release: the patch may expose what its translation call returns, and changes nothing it does.
items.ask: Does the command rebuild the copy from the released crate's source and the patch files without the network, and fail on one changed byte? Read the patch: outside the passthrough shader path, does it do more than expose the translation call's existing results?

work_packages.quality_bar: Launch as a shipped Metal game prepares it, following Apple's guidance to build GPU binaries ahead of time: the shaders the game needs were compiled when it was built, they are exactly the ones the running game asks for, and a library that does not match is rebuilt before play and never during it.

work_packages.name: A warm launch compiles no pipeline: the local pipeline archive is proved by a strict fresh-process run

items.statement: The pinned backend's second patch backs wgpu's pipeline cache with a Metal binary archive: pipelines created with the cache are added to the archive, and its data survives a write to a file and a read in a new process. The archive change is its own patch file beside WP10's, and D10.6's pin check passes with both.
items.ask: Is the archive change one patch a reader can review apart from WP10's? Does any shipping path write the archive during play?

items.statement: The strict warm witness passes: a fresh process opens the archive read-only, with harvest, write-back and compilation on a miss all off so that a miss is an error, creates every pipeline of the manifest and reaches readiness. The same witness fails on an empty archive and on one that lacks a single pipeline of the manifest. Harvest is a separate command.
items.ask: Is a miss made an error by Metal's own option on the pipeline, not by a counter read afterwards? Are the two failing cases run by the same command as the passing one?

items.statement: An archive with a stale key, one whose payload is corrupted at the same length, and a valid archive that holds only part of the manifest each end in a game that reaches readiness and plays the route with no pipeline compiled during play. Each is counted by its cause, apart from device errors.

Launch-to-ready on the final manifest is on record for WGSL in series, cooked libraries prepared in parallel, and the archive, cold and warm, under stated cache conditions, from two separate runs of each with build and load. The path the game takes by default is the one the record shows fastest, chosen through the registry. No time decides the result.
items.ask: Does the default follow the record, and can each path still be forced for a comparison?

work_packages.quality_bar: A warm start as a shipped Metal game with binary archives has it: the second launch compiles nothing, a damaged or outdated archive costs one slower launch and never a crash or a hitch in play, and the proof is a run that is not allowed to fall back.

work_packages.name: Apple tile with MetalFX and EDR is compared with portable TAAU on the route, and G4 closes

items.statement: Paired route rows compare the Apple recipe with MetalFX and EDR against the portable recipe with TAAU, SDR at H = 1, on this Mac, alternating, under one replayed scale trace. They record GPU pass and segment times, display ticks without a present and present intervals, the governor's trace, creation counters by thread and phase, the colour difference to the reference, graph-declared traffic and measured traffic (or the word unmeasured) at two scales, the cost of the float drawable on an SDR display, and the recipe and registry digest, with build and load.
items.ask: Are the two arms run alternately in one session from the same commit and scale trace? Is every row either a figure with its conditions or marked as not measured, with none left blank?

items.statement: In Chrome the route runs with TAAU, dynamic scale and the governor on, at the canvas's backing size, and creates nothing after the page reports ready.

On the iPhone simulator the game runs reconstruction and the SDR path at the surface's extent through a rotation and a trip to the background and back. Function only: the evidence says that iPhone EDR and timing are owed.
The registry's default reconstructor on the Apple recipe is the one the paired record supports, recorded as promotion evidence, and every tripwire this module raised has an assigned follow-up.
items.ask: Which reconstructor does the Apple recipe resolve by default at the closing commit, and which rows of D11.1's record support that? List each open tripwire and where its follow-up is written.

items.statement: Gate G4 holds as the brief words it, on the evidence the design's closing table names, and the maturity ledger says what was and was not proved, with implementation, correctness, visuals and device results apart. EDR is recorded as values above SDR white given to a layer configured for EDR, not as light the panel emitted. The physical iPhone and external-display rows are named as owed.
items.ask: Take the brief's G4 sentence clause by clause: which item of WP3 to WP12 proves each, and is any clause proved only by a forced override that the ledger does not label?

items.statement: In real time on the Mac's Apple recipe, with MetalFX, EDR and the governor on at full screen, the route is sharp and stable: clean edges on the terrain silhouette and thin props, steady stars, no ghost behind a moving prop, no brightness lag through the time-of-day scrub, and no hitch.
items.inspect: Capture the route with T2 engine capture in `realtime` mode at the built-in display's pixel size, with capture's own cost shown apart. Watch it at 1x, then judge native-size crops at each stop. Say that you watched motion.

items.statement: In real time in Chrome the route under TAAU with the governor on is sharp and stable in the same places.
items.inspect: Capture the route with T2 engine capture in `realtime` mode in Chrome and judge the same crops. Note any stop where Chrome differs from the Mac.

items.statement: The owner's look at EDR on the built-in display is asked for and recorded as an observation that gates nothing. The evidence page says how to see EDR on and off at the sunset and night-lights stops and what to note. The ledger carries the observation's status, outstanding or the owner's words with the display's brightness and headroom at the time, apart from what agents proved.
items.ask: Does the evidence page carry the request, and the ledger its status, kept apart from the agent and device evidence? Does any sentence there, or in the closing report, offer captured values as proof of what the panel emits, or make G4's close wait for the owner?

work_packages.quality_bar: The whole presentation path at the level of a shipped high-end Mac game: sharp and stable at the display's full resolution, highlights above SDR white in the frame the XDR display's surface is given, the display's rate held, and no hitch or compile during play, with the Apple path's win over the portable one measured and not assumed.
